consensus_summary: The helmet of salvation is the believer's assurance and/or eschatological hope of salvation, received as God's gift, which protects the mind and thoughts against doubt, despair, and demonic attack in spiritual warfare. All responses cite Eph 6:17, 1 Thess 5:8, and Isa 59:17 (God as divine warrior) as the source imagery, with acknowledged secondary readings: divine-warrior armor bestowed on believers, and (as a minority patristic view) the helmet as Christ himself.
book_summary: The helmet is salvation covering the head, identified with Christ who is 'the Head' (1 Cor 11:3). It is God's own armor lent to His people, and it protects the head/forehead specifically as the place where true or counterfeit allegiance is marked (Rev 22:4).
consensus_core_identification: Salvation—chiefly the believer's assurance or hope of it—functioning as God-given protection of the mind in spiritual conflict.
book_core_identification: Christ Himself (the Head) as God's own armor lent to believers, covering the head as the site where allegiance to God or to the counterfeit is marked.
boundary_disagreement: The book shifts the referent from the believer's subjective assurance/hope to the objective person of Christ as the protecting covering, elevating what the consensus lists only as a minority alternative (salvation = Christ; divine-warrior armor transferred). It also reclassifies what is being protected: not the mind/thought-life (the consensus's dominant emphasis) but the head as the locus of allegiance-marking, connecting the helmet to the forehead-seal motif of Rev 22:4—a case-space no consensus response includes.
rationale: The book's identification is recognizably within the consensus family: it combines two listed alternatives—the divine-warrior reading (God's own armor from Isa 59:17 bestowed/lent to His people) and the Christological reading (the helmet as Christ, noted as a minority patristic view in Response A). Because these are acknowledged strands, the book is not NOVEL and does not replace the central referent (salvation as God-given protective armor). However, it materially sharpens and re-centers the meaning: the head is protected because Christ is 'the Head' (1 Cor 11:3 wordplay), and the protection concerns allegiance-marking on the forehead (Rev 22:4), displacing the consensus's dominant 'protection of the mind/assurance against doubt' emphasis. This is real boundary and emphasis disagreement within a shared category, fitting REFINED with a partial reclassification of covered cases.
strongest_objection: One could argue DIVERGENT: the consensus's central identification is the believer's assurance/hope of salvation guarding the mind, whereas the book identifies the helmet with Christ Himself and with an allegiance-marking function—arguably a replacement of the psychological-assurance referent rather than a refinement. The Rev 22:4 forehead-mark connection in particular has no footing in any consensus response, and 1 Cor 11:3's 'Head' wordplay is a homiletical link rather than exegetical support, so the citations only partially warrant the book's distinctive claims.
